title: Rethinking Hate Speech Detection on Social Media: Can LLMs Replace Traditional Models?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating and comparing the classification accuracy of traditional transformer models versus Large Language Models (LLMs) on code-mixed and transliterated Hindi-English text to test robustness and performance disparities across informal linguistic variations.

Analyzing the targets of hate speech within the IndoHateMix, HateXplain, and ImplicitHate datasets to evaluate the models' ability to detect hostility and stereotypes directed at religious communities such as Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, and Jews.

Benchmarking models on the ImplicitHate and HateXplain datasets to assess their capability in detecting subtle, implicit stereotypes and explicit hateful language directed at racial and ethnic groups like African Americans and Mexicans.
Examining hate speech detection capabilities on the IndoHateMix dataset involving attacks, frustration, and targeted negative sentiment directed at specific political figures and leaders.
